Twenty Third Indian Antarctic Expedition
Ministry o f Earth Sciences, Technical Publication No. 21, pp 173-190
Studies on Diatom Flora of Schirmacher Oasis, East
Antarctica
M. Palanisamy
Botanical Survey o f India 
Andaman Circle, Port Blair- 744 102
ABSTRACT
The D iatom  flora o f Schirm acher Oasis, East A ntarctica was investigated 
during XXIIIrd  (2003-2004) Indian Scientific Expedition to Antarctica. An assessment 
o f the diversity o f diatom flora o f Schirmacher Oasis resulted in a total o f 18 species, 
representing 11 genera o f which Achnanthes  (2), Fragilaria  (3), Synedra (\), Luticola  
(2), Navicula  (3), Stauroneis  (1), D iadesm is(  1), Pinnularia(  1), Gam phomema(  1), 
Hantzschia(  1) and Nitzschia(2) . O f 18 taxa found, 8 were first time for E. Antarctica. 
This paper deals the taxonom ical description o f all diatom. This study reveals that 
the species com position o f diatoms are m ore in the W estern part than the Eastern 
part o f the Schirm acher Oasis. Pinnularia, Navicula, Luticola, N itzschia  and 
H antzschia  w ere abundant in Schirm acher Oasis.
INTRODUCTION
The first systematic exploration of the Polar water of Antarctica was 
conducted by Englishman James Cook who circumnavigated Antarctica 
twice between 1772 and 1775. After that a number of investigations were 
made to explored diversity of marine coastal vertebrates, phytoplankton, 
and several workers studied distribution and taxonomical evaluation of 
algal flora of different places of Antarctic ice continent by West and West 
(1911), Fritsch,F.E.(1912), Komarek and Ruzicka (1966), Parker et 
a/. (1972), Hirano (1979), Broady (1982), Howard Williams et al.( 1986) 
and Hawes (1988). Since then about 700 algal taxa have been reported 
from the Antarctic continent by Pankow et al. 1991. A detailed study of 
diversity, distribution and dispersal of Antarctic terrestrial algae was given 
by Broady (1996). The investigation on diatom flora also made from varies 
part of Antarctica by Fukushima (1962),Ohtani (1986), Andreoli et al (1995), 
Jones (1996), Kawecka and Olech,. (1993) and Temniskova-Topalova et 
al (1999).

174 M. Palanisamy
Schirmacher Oasis in particular has also attracted considerable attention 
from the point of view of algal studies (Aleshinskaya and Bardin, 
1965;Komarek and Ruzicka, 1966; Simonov,1971; and Pankow 
et al., 1987).Altogether some 63 taxa were reported. However, Kashyap, 
1988; Pandey et al., 1995; Pandey and Kashyap, 1995;Gupta & Kashyap, 
1998; Shukla et al., 1997, 1999 were studied the Algal flora of Schirmacher 
Oasis. Most of the work is mainly confined to morphology, floristic, physiology, 
nutrient status, life cycle and diversity of Blue green algae only. Gupta (2002) 
reported 10 diatom species from schirmacher Oasis. Attention has paid to 
Bacilolariophyceae, Chlorophyceae, Chrysophyceae, Dinophyceae and 
Dinophyceae were very meager. It is thus apparent that a considerable 
lacuna in the study of algal diversity of Schirmacher Oasis in general, except 
for the Cyanophycean elements still persist from Indian point of view. It 
was felt that a comprehensive but concise compilation is a requirement. 
The present program therefore is an attempt to bring together the basic 
way of identification and documentation of all diatoms belonging to many of 
the genera and species occurred abundantly and commonly in fresh water 
ecosystems of Schirmacher Oasis, East Antarctica.
Diatoms are single celled algae of the class Bacillariophyceae. The 
skeleton of a diatom or frustule is made of very pure silica. This skeleton is 
divided in to two parts, one of which (epitheca) overlaps the other 
(hypotheca) like the lid of box or petridish. Ditoms extremely abundant in 
aquatic ecosystems, it is estimated the 20% to 25% of all organic carbon 
fixed on the planet is carried out by diatoms (Werner, 1977). Diatoms are 
thus a major food resource for aquatic microorganisms and animal larvae, 
and are a major source of atmospheric oxygen. Diatoms are also used for 
water quality evaluation (Almedia,1998). The silicified cell wall gives a 
beautiful look. Diatomaceous earth, a substance composed of fossil diatoms, 
is used for making filters, insulation, abrasives, paints, etc.
STUDY AREA
Schirmacher Oasis (70° 44’  S to 11°54’E) is a group of low lying -  
hills, essentially snow and ice-free high polar rock desert in the Eastern 
Droning Maud Land, East Antarctica(Fig.l). It is 70 km away from Prince 
Astrid Coast. The Oasis oriented in east -  west direction, lies between two 
types of large ice bodies viz., glacier in the south and ice shelf at the north 
of the Oasis. It covers an area of about 34 km2 . The altitudes lie between
